scenarios.evidence: L=R with lagging P replays. Missing/ambiguous cursors do not borrow another repo. Missing objects, shallow history, and ancestry-command errors are distinct from rewrite. Qualified merge DAGs replay in deterministic oldest-first topological order when the full frontier fits in one batch; merge-DAG backlogs beyond the cap continue in explicit oldest-first batches with durable git_replay_continuation state (handled commit set plus pinned admitted R) across restart. Legacy seeded unsupported_merge_dag durable blocks still refuse. Linear backlogs over 1000 continue in explicit oldest-first batches of at most 1000 commits per cycle; the handled Git checkpoint and durable continuation record are the restart cursor. While linear continuation is incomplete the bridge resets only through the current batch tip, conflict detection uses the full admitted P→R path and fails closed on partial coverage, and pending SVN file deltas defer the cycle with no bridge reset or writes while SVN-only metadata revisions drain without starving Git batches. Pending selection is hide/push P..R; the older-side engine replay proof is candidate_r10_merge_dag_older_side_replayed_with_delta; merge-DAG multi-batch continuation proof is candidate_r10_merge_dag_continuation_batched and cap=1/2 siblings plus candidate_r10_merge_dag_continuation_batched_distinct_trees_cap1/cap3, candidate_r66_merge_dag_continuation_survives_restart, and candidate_r66_merge_dag_continuation_missing_row_idempotent; conflict-coverage gate proof is candidate_r66_incomplete_conflict_coverage_fail_closed; SVN-only drain proof is candidate_r66_drain_git_batch_past_svn_only; visited-order skip proof is pending_frontier::visited_order_truncation_skips_older_pending_side. Durable UnsupportedHistory blocks (merge DAG and legacy backlog) survive restart; fetch_git_changes persists the same record on second-line UnsupportedHistory. Personal-mode merge-DAG containment is proven under R09/R66 personal cases. Policy/receipt supporting cases belong to the #63 compatibility reader.

scenarios.title: Two independent repos with overlapping revisions and names

scenarios.evidence: A two-pair engine fixture keeps repository cursors scoped and leaves an unrelated healthy pair runnable while one is blocked. The pinned old-import inventory keeps two r2 imports and a disabled third repository distinct. The svnserve real-engine suite imports two repos concurrently at the same numeric SVN revision and branch name without checkpoint, job, or credential crossover; R17_SVNSERVE_CONCURRENT_OVERLAP requires overlapping SyncEngine cycle windows, peak concurrent in-flight imports, and at least one successful import finishing while a peer cycle is still active (active-cycle oracle latched across lock-retry sleeps, not merely post-hoc in_flight sampling). R17_SVNSERVE_CONCURRENT_CREDENTIAL_RELOAD requires both repo labels in-flight before a scoped alpha kv rewrite, proves the overlapping import keeps its construction-time svn password, and proves a later cycle reloads rotated svnserve/kv credentials with queried sync_records mapping for post-reload.txt without beta crossover (emits PARTIAL when overlap, mapping, or reload cannot be shown). R17_SVNSERVE_PARENT_CHILD_CONCURRENT_CREDENTIAL_RELOAD pairs repo_beta under repo_alpha with a keyless child svn chain, rewrites parent scoped secrets during overlapping imports, keeps teams_webhook_url rows isolated, and reloads rotated parent credentials for a child import with child-post-chain-reload.txt bridge-tree, post-cycle password marker, and mapping checks when overlap is shown. R17_SVNSERVE_NOTIFICATION_ISOLATION runs concurrent svnserve imports with distinct per-repo teams_webhook_url values and records PARTIAL when no Notifier delivery is observed (only teams_webhook_url persistence plus sync_status and audit_log confinement, not crossed webhook delivery). RS-11 team cases prove per-repo git/svn canary reload across two independent repos with a contaminating global key: rotation on one repo does not change the sibling, reopen reloads the scoped value, explicit revocation clears embedded git credentials without global fallback, missed lookups preserve in-memory and URL-embedded secrets, legacy CLI config passwords survive reload without kv_state keys, and a revoked parent blocks global fallback for a keyless child. Scheduler and import credential prep preserve URL-embedded git tokens on chain miss or kv_state lookup failure; explicit per-repo revocation strips embedded git tokens on the scheduler path. Daemon startup and setup import/reset-reimport apply only config/env credentials to the legacy config remote, CLI sync now without a repo id does not keep a managed-repo token there, and explicit child revocations survive startup seeding plus a scheduler cycle.
